messages.text: What evidence is required to compare our Oscilloscope solution with a competitor for Automotive without making unsupported claims?

To compare our Oscilloscope solution with a competitor for Automotive, the evidence must include a cited source that directly connects all relevant facets: the oscilloscope solution, the competitor, and the Automotive application; separate co-mentions are insufficient for a comparison or recommendation [68].
Formal R&S oscilloscope specifications / features / configuration evidence for the exact product and options being compared, because competitive pages or sales positioning cannot replace formal specifications or features documents [20].
Competitor official datasheets, release notes, support terms, or third-party evidence to verify competitor frequency range, bandwidth, software tools, support model, and other technical claims [62].
External verification for any R&S-internal battle-card claims about a competitor, because such descriptions need competitor official data or third-party validation [11].
Avoid treating “only platform,” “leadership,” “lower TCO,” “fewer boxes,” or similar sales language as verified technical specifications [20].
If making claims such as “industry’s only,” “fully integrated,” “long-term scalability,” or similar, those require formal datasheets, features documents, conformance reports, or configuration-tool evidence [21].
Automotive linkage must be explicitly supported; the available Automotive / UAV oscilloscope index only shows a Taiwan UAV R&S solution-mapping page, not a supported Automotive oscilloscope-vs-competitor comparison [12].
